items.title: Gucci Unveils New Store Concept on Avenue Montaigne in Paris
items.summary: WWD covers Gucci's new flagship at 56 Avenue Montaigne, the first global rollout of 'The Store Show' concept previewed at Gucci's September Milan show, designed by Demna and Francesca Bellettini with a private 'Appartamento' client space.

items.title: Gucci ridisegna il retail a Parigi: il nuovo flagship di Avenue Montaigne
items.summary: Italian trade outlet details the 1,480 sqm, four-floor Paris flagship's materials (Ceppo di Gre stone, travertino, Victoria Regia marble) and its 'show and hide' display philosophy; frames it as the first concrete expression of Gucci's retail evolution under Demna, without commentary on Kering's financial results.

items.title: Gucci avenue Montaigne : la boutique comme suite de pieces
items.summary: French trade analysis takes a skeptical tone on the new boutique, questioning whether the theatrical room-by-room design will keep merchandise visible and whether the concept is scalable beyond this single flagship, treating it as creative experimentation rather than confirmed retail innovation.

items.title: Gucci se revele sous un nouveau jour sur l'avenue Montaigne

items.title: Avenue Montaigne, Gucci transforme son flagship parisien en Store Show
items.summary: French luxury trade title frames the new flagship as Gucci literally transplanting its runway 'Store Show' concept into physical retail, highlighting the second-floor Appartamento as a tool for courting top-tier clients amid Gucci's broader sales slump.

items.title: At the LACMA Art+Film Gala 2026, Demna's Gucci Steps Into the Spotlight

items.title: LACMA's Star-Studded Art+Film Gala Raises Nearly $7 M.
